memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"The people remained at a distance, while Moses approached the thick darkness
where God was." - Ex 20:21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
One sentence, and a whole picture. The people stood back. Moses walked in.

Notice where God was: in the thick darkness. Not in a shining, obvious place, but
in the dark cloud where nothing could be seen clearly.

That is worth sitting with. We often assume God is found where things are bright
and clear, and that darkness means He is absent. Here the darkness is precisely
where He is.

Many believers have discovered this. Seasons of confusion, grief, or unanswered
questions are not necessarily seasons of God's absence. Sometimes He is nearest
when we can see least.

Notice also what it took for Moses to walk in. Everyone else stayed back, and
that was not unreasonable. Moses went toward the thing that frightened everyone.

He could do that because he knew who was in there. Fear of the unknown is
different from approaching the known God in the dark.

Job, who had every reason to complain about darkness, said, "But he knows the way
that I take; when he has tested me, I will come forth as gold" (Job 23:10).

You may not see. That does not mean He is not there.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you in a dark stretch where you have assumed God is absent?
2. What would it look like to walk toward God rather than wait for clarity?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, when I cannot see, help me to walk toward You anyway. Thank You that You
are present even in the darkness. Amen.
